question: If independent extremophiles are aligned by entry into and exit from their survival state rather than by absolute time, does a common resolution architecture appear?

alignment.NORMAL: ordinary active state before major stress
alignment.ENTRY: transition into stress-adapted or dormant state
alignment.SURVIVAL_STATE: active homeostatic adaptation or metabolically suppressed protected state
alignment.RECOVERY: damage processing, biochemical normalization, structural restoration
alignment.RESUMED_FUNCTION: growth, movement, photosynthesis or replication resumes

initial_hypotheses.claim: Extreme survival requires continuous active repair throughout the extreme state.
initial_hypotheses.why: Dormant spores and anhydrobiotes can accumulate damage while metabolism is minimal or absent and execute substantial repair only on germination/rehydration.

initial_hypotheses.claim: A reversible dormant state is the universal extremophile strategy.
initial_hypotheses.why: Psychrophiles, halophiles, acidophiles, alkaliphiles, piezophiles, osmophiles and many thermophiles remain metabolically active under their defining extreme.

initial_hypotheses.claim: Preventing DNA damage is the central sufficient extremophile mechanism.
initial_hypotheses.why: Deinococcus and other radiotolerant models show that proteome protection, ROS control and post-damage repair are critical; substantial DNA damage can coexist with survival.

initial_hypotheses.claim: Lower metabolism is sufficient for extreme survival and therefore a general longevity mechanism.
initial_hypotheses.why: Many extremophiles actively grow under extremes; dormant-state duration can also reduce recovery probability in tardigrades.

ACTIVE_HOMEOSTASIS.architecture: SENSE EXTREME -> continuously tune membrane/solvent/proteome/redox/metabolism -> repair damage while functioning -> maintain viable operating state
ACTIVE_HOMEOSTASIS.core_rule: Keep biochemistry inside a workable envelope instead of leaving the active state.

members: Ramazzottius varieornatus and other anhydrobiotic tardigrades
REVERSIBLE_SUSPENSION_RECOVERY.architecture: SENSE/ENTER -> suppress vulnerable processes -> physically/chemically stabilize -> tolerate residual damage -> REENTRY -> prioritized repair/normalization -> resume function
REVERSIBLE_SUSPENSION_RECOVERY.core_rule: Preserve enough structure and repair capacity to make a controlled return possible.

kinetic_cases.kinetics: Germination begins on the scale of minutes; damaged DNA is processed during germination/outgrowth, with published work placing important repair in the early ~15-60 min revival window depending on lesion/system.
kinetic_cases.critical_observation: Repair capacity is prepared before dormancy but much lesion processing waits until rehydration/metabolism resumes.

kinetic_cases.kinetics: DNA DSB repair measured at 0/2/8/24/48 h after rehydration; early repair transcription peaks around ~1.5 h in later transcriptomic work; mobility can recover before genome integrity is fully restored.
kinetic_cases.critical_observation: Functional recovery and molecular repair are partially decoupled; EXIT is not one instant.

kinetic_cases.kinetics: Animals can revive rapidly; rehydration produces a strong oxidative pulse that damages DNA, proteins and membrane lipids, yet reported damage is repaired within hours. Earlier work reports full genome-integrity restoration on a longer ~96-h scale for some DSB measurements.
kinetic_cases.critical_observation: Reentry itself is a dangerous transition requiring active recovery, not merely passive rehydration.

kinetic_cases.survival_state: active radiotolerant tardigrade / stress recovery comparison
kinetic_cases.kinetics: TUNEL-detectable DNA damage decreases significantly during 24 h after a well-tolerated extreme radiation dose.
kinetic_cases.critical_observation: Resistance includes damage repair after exposure rather than perfect shielding.

kinetic_cases.kinetics: In ultrastructural work, movement resumes around ~5 min after rehydration; cellular ultrastructure is sampled at 5 and 15 min, illustrating extremely fast functional re-entry in this species.
kinetic_cases.critical_observation: Very fast behavioral recovery does not prove all molecular damage is repaired at that time.

kinetic_cases.kinetics: Recovery is scored at 2/6/24/48 h; longer or repeated anhydrobiosis lowers and delays recovery, and age is a major predictor.
kinetic_cases.critical_observation: Dormancy is not cost-free or infinitely protective; recovery competence itself ages/declines.

kinetic_cases.kinetics: Dehydration-specific products decline during early rehydration; transcriptome after ~24 h clusters near hydrated state, and photosynthetic carbon assimilation substantially recovers over ~48 h.
kinetic_cases.critical_observation: Recovery is an orchestrated state transition, not simple reversal of dehydration.

kinetic_cases.kinetics: Survival and genome recovery after prolonged dry/space exposure are established, while the detailed omics of rehydration/recovery remain explicitly unresolved in a 2026 comparative-genomics study.
kinetic_cases.critical_observation: This is a high-value open dataset/model for testing the recovery architecture.

hard_survivors: Damage must be limited enough that recovery machinery itself remains functional.
Proteome and membrane/solvent integrity are first-class survival variables, not secondary to DNA.
Genome repair is widespread but can occur during stress or be deferred until recovery depending on life strategy.
In reversible-dormancy systems, re-entry is an active regulated phase with its own hazards and repair requirements.
Dormancy protects but is not free: duration, repetition and organismal age can reduce successful recovery.

new_candidate.name: REACTIVATION_REPAIR_CHECKPOINT
new_candidate.formula: PROTECT -> PAUSE_WHEN_NEEDED -> PRESERVE_REPAIR_CAPACITY -> REENTRY -> REPAIR_AND_NORMALIZE -> THEN_FULL_RESUMPTION
new_candidate.why_it_matters: It adds a temporal ordering principle to LONGEVITY SURVIVOR: preserving repair capacity and controlling restart may be as important as the amount of repair machinery.
new_candidate.claim_ceiling: Functional convergence across distant lineages does not establish homologous molecular control or applicability to mammals.

relation_to_mammalian_resolution_gate.similarity: Both architectures emphasize that a temporary stress/repair state must transition into a stable functional state rather than remain indefinitely activated.
relation_to_mammalian_resolution_gate.difference: Extremophile dormancy/re-entry concerns organismal or cellular stress survival, whereas mammalian wound resolution concerns multicellular tissue reconstruction, lineage routing, ECM and fibrosis.

next_killer_tests.test: Build normalized recovery curves for Bacillus spore repair, Adineta DSB recovery, Polypedilum oxidative-damage recovery, tardigrade activity recovery and Craterostigma transcriptome/physiology recovery using tau=0 at rehydration/germination.
Separate behavioral/functional recovery from genome/proteome/ECM or structural recovery; test whether visible function routinely precedes complete molecular repair.
Identify whether full replication/growth is delayed until a damage threshold is cleared in independent dormancy systems; if not, kill the stronger REPAIR_BEFORE_REPLICATION form of the hypothesis.
Use Chroococcidiopsis 2026 recovery data gap as an external prediction: expect rapid rehydration induction of DNA repair/ROS management before full photosynthetic growth.
Compare active-homeostasis extremophiles against dormancy-enabled extremophiles to determine whether proteome preservation predicts tolerance more consistently than DNA-break avoidance.
